product_scope: itpay is the single public Buyer CLI entry point, and $itpay is its user-facing Skill invocation. It covers services, railway planning and booking, orders, authorized purchased content and refunds.
title: Install And Identify The ItPay Agent Runtime
purpose: Install once in a permitted persistent location and enable the same-package Skill. For a new task, prefer the official pinned ItPay CLI when execution is permitted and available in the current host. Install only through the host-permitted official installation path when authorized. Services tasks use the Services Skill; API tasks use the independent API Skill and `itpay api`. CLI calls HTTP APIs directly, never MCP transport. Without permitted CLI capability, use the corresponding ItPay-hosted user Services MCP or Hub MCP and only its actually available tools; ordinary users do not self-host another MCP. Platform-required workflows and explicit connection tests follow the actual available capability. Entry selection never authorizes a permission bypass: preserve the original identity, entry, request/run and current grant after acceptance or an unknown result. Continue across entries only when the owner explicitly supports recovery under the same actual authority; CLI errors never license a substitute transaction or raw HTTP workaround.
when_to_use: The CLI is being installed or upgraded.
The agent needs to confirm its stable runtime identity and default output Host.
current_flow: Use the authorized channel/Backend and host-permitted tool prefix/cache/state directories. Use real dot or muse in those hosts, never codex spoofing. Retain one launcher and its Backend, Agent Type and ITPAY_STATE_DIR for every next/recovery command. Do not change HOME.

Declare the actual host type via ITPAY_AGENT_TYPE or the global --agent-type option, then run itpay setup --json once after installation/upgrade. Preserve that real declaration, launcher/PATH, Backend and any custom private ITPAY_STATE_DIR for all later commands. Exported values can be inherited by child processes; a new shell may need them again. A one-time setup flag is not persistent configuration. setup_ready means device preparation; login_required is a separate valid account status.
Read itpay skill show itpay --json and enable that exact package Skill via the host mechanism. Record the actual path and limitation if the host cannot enable it.
Do not repeat setup, installation or login for ordinary tasks. A nonzero install is not ready; keep the actual error and follow its current recovery.

ITPAY_STATE_DIR selects the private state directory; choose an allowed directory before first enrollment and preserve it. If an existing identity lacks its key or becomes inaccessible, recover access; never rotate identity to regain quota.

Check install prefix, npm cache, state and receipt writes independently. A writable directory is not proof of persistence across sessions. setup reports Skill readability separately from writing, host discovery and version; do not reinstall during normal tasks.

When login_required, the returned account_action is optional: use it only for a user-requested login or an account-required feature; do not auto-login or bind for free queries. Missing host declaration is technical input the Agent restores from actual context, not an unknown server authorization or a reason to ask the human to guess a type.
